audit_after: the cost-of-capital lever. THIS REBUILD IS MOSTLY RECORD-SHAPE AND THAT IS THE REASON THE AUDIT POINT SITS WHERE IT DOES. Of the exemplar's outstanding entries, nine close by committing a record the sanctioned modules already emit — the driver lines, the asset base, the anchor ordering, the rebuild ledger itself — and NONE OF THOSE CAN MOVE THE CENTRAL, because under [R-LENS-03] the class primary IS the central and a record commit does not touch the cash-flow lens. The circularity-block unit correction feeds a CROSS-CHECK, which by the same rule is published beside the answer and never averaged into it. So exactly one lever has a route to the number: rebuilding the cost of capital through cost_of_capital.py, which moves the discount rate and therefore the DCF. The place to stop and look is after that lever and BEFORE the document is rebuilt — because once a figure is written into a delivered document the next reader takes it as settled, and because the terminal is STOPPED (TERMINAL_EVIDENCE_05-09-2026.md, three independent disclosure gaps), so the single largest construction in this study is NOT among the levers and cannot offset whatever the discount rate does.

stopped.why: STOPPED, not deferred. TERMINAL_EVIDENCE_05-09-2026.md records three independent reasons the accounts yield no usable life: dry-docking is capitalised and amortised over two to five years while the vessel line is not split by component; one vessel class prints its age as an unfilled placeholder; and 97.85% of depreciable net book value sits in a single column spanning six disclosed lives from 2 to 40 years. A LIFE THIS DESK CHOSE IS NOT A DISCLOSED LIFE (SIGCM clause 1), so this rebuild does not touch the terminal and the ratchet entry stands.
